# Packaged read-only drain source correction

This three-path source packet corrects independently established acceptance-harness races around the existing in-flight schema-read shutdown check. It does not establish the exact R6 failure cause. R6 completed twenty checks, then failed in inflight-schema-shutdown while the original worker, PostgreSQL and Temporal containers were running without OOM. No exact final guard was retained. Its only logged PostgreSQL schema lock timeout matches the earlier successful outage check; no final-phase timeout or SIGTERM marker was retained. R7 attempted to build the diagnostic successor but hit its storage floor before any runtime acceptance. Those failed receipts remain unchanged.

The native sweep does a fresh schema check on each pass through a transaction with its existing five-second local lock timeout. No successful schema cache explains the final absence. The harness previously treated schedule.trigger(SKIP) acknowledgement as sufficient before looking for a new SQL waiter. That API acknowledgement does not establish a new accepted run, and a recent completed workflow does not establish that the scheduler has drained its runningActions. It also launched separate cold SDK containers between native activity start, SQL observation and post-signal observation. Their startup latency consumes the same bounded schema-read window. These source races exist independently of the unproved R6 trigger.

The correction opens one positively owned read-only Temporal control container before acquiring the schema blocker. It uses the same built image, isolated network, private TLS custody, fixed namespace and schedule, nonroot uid 10001, dropped capabilities, read-only filesystem, memory/CPU/PID bounds and mounted owned private data/TLS volumes as the existing acceptance clients. It has no host port, host source mount, Docker socket, replacement activity or privileged client. Its initial ready frame confirms transport setup only. Container label and running-state readback separately confirm ownership before the held boundary.

The warm client accepts only bounded sequenced canonical frames for observe, idle, triggerActivity, activity, history and close. Fixed owned workflow/run/activity syntax, strict field sets, response sequence/action checks, ASCII/size limits, finite command count, request deadlines, a total session lifetime and explicit close/exit checks prevent arbitrary RPC or diagnostic payloads. Raw stdout and stderr never enter evidence or error messages. Unexpected, duplicate, malformed, out-of-order, unknown-field or over-limit replies fail. The session has one triggerActivity action and pins its actual returned identity internally for later activity/history reads. An ordinary trigger acknowledgement cannot produce started evidence.

Before the blocker, idle admission requires the exact existing schedule, a current completed owned result and zero runningActions. Immediately before the final trigger, the same warm client repeats that scheduler admission. It then verifies a different actual run with one genuinely STARTED sweepReconcilePass on the original worker identity, attempt one and maximum attempts one. A temporarily unscheduled or queued activity is only a waiting state inside the bounded observation loop; it never satisfies the returned proof. Overlap skip, failure to drain, missing start, malformed metadata, wrong worker, changed attempt or replay refusal cannot fall through to success.

The existing independent PostgreSQL observer must still find exactly one query from the original worker container address blocked by the exact owned schema lock, with distinct observer, waiter and blocker PIDs. SIGTERM is sent only after both the actual started activity and this held SQL boundary are observed. The post-signal read uses the warm authenticated client and the same pinned workflow/run/activity identity. It must still be STARTED, and a fresh SQL observer must still see the same waiter and blocker with a different observer PID. A completed, queued or substituted activity after the signal refuses the check. Worker exit zero, non-OOM ownership readback and lifecycle output privacy are unchanged.

After drain, the retained native history must still contain exactly one scheduled, started and completed activity, each linked by its original event IDs and original worker identity, with no failed, timed-out, cancelled, cancellation-requested or retried activity. Its result must be the existing prerequisites_unavailable deferral. The warm client must close successfully and exit zero before the harness proceeds to an independent fresh worker/pass. Existing read-refusal authority stays byte-bound across the three independent observer connections. All twenty-two required check identities, negative TLS/authentication cases, schema/polling/outage assertions, actual entrypoints and ownership-safe resource cleanup remain intact. The new control container is recorded in the same created-resource inventory before launch and removed only through the existing label-checked cleanup. Cleanup failure still fails the whole acceptance result.

The scope remains a read-only prerequisite drain. sqlActivityAttributionProven, providerMutationAccepted, consumedApprovalPreservationProven and receiptRecoveryProven remain false. A SQL waiter and Temporal started metadata do not establish an accepted provider mutation, preserve a consumed browser approval, establish effect receipts, or prove uncertain cloud-write recovery. Those production requirements remain open. No default API/server, provider/cloud operation, arbitrary native start, parallel execution engine or authority constructor was added.

The owned regression suite retains all existing case identities and assertions. Additive tests exercise the exact read/control closure against explicit modeled locked-SDK replies, plus strict scalar request/response framing. They cover drained-action waiting, genuine-start predicates, overlap skip, never-drained state, queued activity, wrong worker, changed attempts, exact held reread, terminal history linkage, malformed/duplicate/foreign/unknown payloads and source lifecycle ordering. These are protocol and source models. They do not execute PostgreSQL, Temporal, TLS, Docker, a real activity or a worker, and cannot substitute for package acceptance. Frozen CASE-CONTRACT.json lists their precise identities and modeled scope.
